correctness.rationale: For every new top simplex of M(H) minus M(G), a uniquely completable codimension-one face containing a forbidden graph edge gives a relative elementary collapse; distinct top simplices cannot share such a face. Thus relative H_(m-1)=0 and relative H_(m-2) is free. The integer long exact sequence proves primitive injectivity. Individual matching complexes similarly collapse their top simplices, giving free H_(m-2). A finite flag of saturated sublattices has an adapted integral basis. An exact 512-/763-face Morse acyclicity replay proves the two 8-vertex sphere ranks and the rank-53 cofiber; exhaustive 45 relative witnesses and the C6 sharpness vector were independently checked. No finite test is substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus meaning searches for the primitive edge-filtration theorem, degree, aliases and concrete 79-to-132 inclusion found no covering assertion; relevant full primary text and closest ledger claim were compared by implication. Jonsson gives a long exact sequence and an unproved all-degree short-exact splitting conjecture for a special complete-graph one-edge situation; the present explicit relative collapse proves the all-graph near-top injection and primitivity. The separate known K8 and cocktail-party homotopy types do not determine their inclusion map. Some older literature may express the elementary relative-collapse argument in an unindexed equivalent form; this is a residual bibliographic risk, not claimed impossible.
residual_risks: A differently named or unindexed preexisting relative-collapse argument could imply the universal split-injectivity lemma; a database nonhit is not a proof of uniqueness.
The full contents of every older matching-complex monograph and thesis have not been examined; subject-matter expert review would strengthen novelty judgment.
No independent scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A natural, previously unresolved integral persistence question is settled uniformly for all graph-edge filtrations at the near-top matching degree, and the hypothesis is shown degree-sharp by an explicit counterexample. The primitive quotient is stronger than a rank comparison: the known 79- and 132-sphere homotopy types do not imply that their natural map splits or that its cofiber has 53 spheres. This theorem supplies a concrete, proved degree-range contribution relevant to Jonsson’s all-degree exact-sequence splitting conjecture without claiming the latter.
